extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: Evaluation benchmark for low-resource and multilingual machine translation consisting of 3001 sentences from English Wikipedia translated into 101 languages, with multilingual alignment and rich metadata.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.inLanguage: English, Afrikaans, Amharic, Arabic, Armenian, Assamese, Asturian, Azerbaijani, Belarusian, Bengali, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Burmese, Catalan, Cebuano, Chinese (Simpl), Chinese (Trad), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Estonian, Filipino (Tagalog), Finnish, French, Fula, Galician, Ganda, Georgian, German, Greek, Gujarati, Hausa, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Igbo, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Javanese, Kabuverdianu, Kamba, Kannada, Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Lao, Latvian, Lingala, Lithuanian, Luo, Luxembourgish, Malay, Malayalam, Maltese, Maori, Macedonian, Marathi, Mongolian, Nepali, Northern Sotho, Nyanja, Occitan, Oriya, Oromo, Pashto, Persian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Shona, Sindhi, Slovak, Slovenian, Somali, Sorani Kurdish, Spanish (Latin America), Swahili, Swedish, Tajik, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Umbundu, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese, Welsh, Wolof, Xhosa, Yoruba, Zulu
extraction.citeAs: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, and Angela Fan. 2021. The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia-related Wikimedia sources, then translated into 101 languages by professional translators through a multi-phase workflow including pilot studies, automatic checks, human quality assurance, and possible re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia via Wikimedia sources: Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sentences were sampled from articles, contiguous sentences were manually selected while avoiding malformed segments, paragraph position was balanced across beginning/middle/end, and metadata such as URL, topic, hyperlinks, and images were extracted.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic quality control checks were applied to translations, including language identification, copy detection from source, length difference checks, fluency checks with a language model, and similarity checks against commercial translation engines; failing translations were sent for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Professional translators translated the sentences, different translators within the same LSP edited them, and an independent evaluation LSP performed human quality assessment using error categories and severity levels. Sentences and articles were also manually labeled for sub-topic metadata.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was analyzed using a Translation Quality Score on a 0–100 scale based on counted error types and severity levels; translations below threshold were re-translated and sometimes re-evaluated by humans.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 human annotation stages per translated item (translation/editing and independent human evaluation), with additional rounds if quality was insufficient
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For sentence selection: 10 annotators in the lab, 6 male and 4 female; roles included researchers and program/project managers; regions included East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Language identification tools, language models for fluency checking, and sentence-level SentencePiece BLEU heuristic against commercial translation engines
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors hope to continue expanding the number of languages covered in FLORES-101; the test set is served through a public evaluation server rather than released directly.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator gender, professional role, and region of origin were described for the sentence selection annotators.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to foster progress in machine translation for low-resource languages, which could benefit speakers of languages underserved by current translation systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential bias from document structure was mitigated by balancing paragraph positions; the authors also discuss possible translationese effects from using English as the sole source language.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: All source sentences come from English, so non-English source sentences are human translations and may exhibit translationese; some candidate languages could not meet the quality threshold and were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use cases are evaluation and benchmarking of many-to-many multilingual machine translation, including dev, devtest, and test splits for hyper-parameter tuning, development testing, and final evaluation. The dataset may also support document-level translation, multimodal translation, classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.

name.evidence: In this work, we introduce the F LORES -101 evaluation benchmark

description.evidence: In this work, we introduce the F LORES -101 evaluation benchmark, consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains. These sentences have been translated in 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The test set will not be released, but will be available via a publicly available evaluation server, while the dev and devtest are publicly downloadable

rai:dataCollection.evidence: To achieve the above goals, the overall construction process consisted of three phases... First, we extracted sentences to translate from English Wikipedia. Second, we designed and ran pilot experiments to determine the translation process, and finally we launched the actual translation workflow for over 100 languages.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources... The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Original Source. All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources... Instead, we opted to source all sentences from English Wikipedia... we collected a third of the sentences from Wikinews... a third from Wikijunior... and a third from WikiVoyage

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. To avoid bias coming from the document structure, we carefully selected one paragraph per document, from either the beginning, middle or end of the article.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We implemented several checks to ensure the first round of translations were of acceptable quality: (i) language identification, (ii) checking whether the translation is a copy of the source sentence; (iii) checking whether the translation has significantly different length, (iv) checking translation fluency according to a language model, (v) and checking whether the translation is a copy of the translation produced by publicly available translation engines.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: These sentences have been translated in 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process... Once sentences are translated, the data is sent to different translators within the LSP for editing... Afterwards, translations are sent to an evaluation LSP that performs quality assessment... We manually labeled all sentences by a more detailed sub-topic, one of 10 possibilities

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: For each language, all source sentences are sent to a certain translation LSPs... Afterwards, translations are sent to an evaluation LSP that performs quality assessment

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We assess translation quality through a Translation Quality Score, calculated per language on a 0 to 100 scale. The translation quality score is determined based on the number of identified errors by the evaluation LSPs... Based on our pilot experiments, we set the acceptable translation quality score to 90%.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Once sentences are translated, the data is sent to different translators within the LSP for editing... Afterwards, translations are sent to an evaluation LSP that performs quality assessment... If the score is below the accepted threshold, translations together with the assessment report are sent back to the translation LSP for re-translation.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: The selection process was performed by 10 different annotators in our lab, 6 male and 4 female; with different roles in research: researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; originally coming from different regions of the world: East Asia, South Asia, Southem Europe, Latin America and North America.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We implemented several checks... (i) language identification... (iv) checking translation fluency according to a language model, (v) and checking whether the translation is a copy of the translation produced by publicly available translation engines.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We hope to continue to expand the number of languages covered in FLORES -101 and make the test set available to various community efforts

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: The selection process was performed by 10 different annotators in our lab, 6 male and 4 female; with different roles in research... originally coming from different regions of the world

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Yet, the majority of the world’s population speak low-resource languages and would benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages... By publicly releasing such a high-quality and high-coverage dataset, we hope to foster progress in the machine translation community and beyond.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: To avoid bias coming from the document structure, we carefully selected one paragraph per document, from either the beginning, middle or end of the article... While translationese (or overly literal or awkward translations) has known idiosyncrasies

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: By translating the same set of English sentences in more than hundred languages, we enable evaluation of multilingual MT with the only caveat that source sentences not in English are produced by human translators... Note that several languages were considered beyond our set of 101, but were unable to meet the bar after rounds of re-translation.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The dev set is meant to be used for hyper-parameter tuning. The devtest is meant to be used for testing purpose during the development phase... FLORES -101 supports many-to-many evaluation... With rich metadata, it also supports multimodal translation via images, and document-level translation... Beyond translation, FLORES -101 can be used to evaluate tasks such as sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.
